page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-64-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-equipped virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes six local NVMe SSDs totaling 2172 GB of capacity. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong computational and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU testing, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is robust, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth reaching 6631.63 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 203.23 GB/sec. Database operations and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top 10%, while Redis SET operations achieve 110.03 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-highmem-64-lssd offers a high-capacity memory profile paired with fast local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring both high memory capacity and low-latency storage without the overhead of external disk attachments. The absence of a GPU limits its applicability for hardware-accelerated machine learning training, but its high memory bandwidth and top-tier database benchmark performance make it highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
